plants.name: Prunus × yedoensis
plants.description: Clouds of pale, almost white-pink blossoms cover bare branches before the leaves appear. Petals drift down like confetti in the spring breeze. The effect is one of the most celebrated sights of the season.
plants.bloomingSeason: Late March to mid-April in lowland Japan. Peak bloom comes later at higher elevations and farther north, so flowers are still opening in northern Honshu and Hokkaido around April 19.
plants.location: Northern Japan (Tohoku and Hokkaido), especially castle parks such as Hirosaki
plants.funFact: Every Yoshino cherry traces back to a single original tree, because the cultivar is propagated by grafting. The trees are genetic clones, so they bloom in near-perfect synchrony.

plants.name: Tulipa gesneriana
plants.description: Cup-shaped blooms in nearly every color stand on smooth, upright stems above blue-green leaves. Whole fields turn into bands of vivid color. They are a symbol of spring across the Netherlands.
plants.bloomingSeason: Early April to early May in the Netherlands, with peak bloom usually in mid to late April
plants.location: Bollenstreek bulb region of the Netherlands, including Lisse and Keukenhof
plants.funFact: Tulips came from the mountains of Central Asia. In the 1630s their bulbs became so valuable in Holland that a single rare bulb could cost more than a house.

plants.name: Colchicum autumnale
plants.description: Goblet-shaped flowers rise from the ground on bare stems.
plants.bloomingSeason: Autumn in the Northern Hemisphere. In the Southern Hemisphere, where April is autumn, it blooms around April.
plants.location: Southern Hemisphere gardens, such as those in New Zealand and southern Australia
plants.funFact: The plant's leaves emerge in spring, long after the flowers have faded. This is why it is nicknamed the naked lady.
